title: Networked Corruption Risks in European Defense Procurement
summary_en: Public defence procurement is exposed to particular corruption risks: classified specifications, narrow supplier pools, and high deal sizes. Czibik, Fazekas and co-authors construct corruption-risk scores for European defence-procurement contracts and analyse them as a network linking buyers, suppliers, and shared agents. They identify clusters of contracts with elevated risk profiles and document cross-border patterns in how risk concentrates within supplier-agent networks. [Volume-chapter summary; abstract not publicly available — verification recommended.]
data_used: TED (Tenders Electronic Daily) European public-procurement micro-data restricted to defence-related contracts, augmented with corruption-risk indicators (single-bidder rates, calls-for-tender wording, anomalous contract values) and constructed buyer-supplier-agent networks.
policy_relevance: Relevant to Hungarian public-procurement integrity policy (Állami Számvevőszék, Integritás Hatóság) and EU defence-procurement governance (DG DEFIS, EDA): the network-based risk-score methodology is directly applicable to Hungarian public tenders, where Fazekas and colleagues have shown elevated risk indicators. Defence procurement is a particular policy hotspot given Hungarian rearmament programmes and EU defence-fund allocations.
